keyFindings.description: resolveCommentRecipients runs before any send and a failed query sets item.failure, which settle backs off before the event's owner topic is published. On main a failed author lookup ran after the owner topic was sent, so the issue subject still got the event in id order (scanBatch's own comment: an event backed off reaches its issue subject after later events, which the Legion daemon drops as stale). And settle checks item.failure before ctx.Err(), so a stopping process backs these events off (attempts+1, ERROR) where every other event is released (TestAnOutboxStoppedMidBatchMarksTheAnsweredAndReleasesTheRest's contract). The claimed 'backs off only the events that needed it' has no test.

The rewrite dropped '(--route '' on release)' while still recommending --route session:<your id>. Releasing a claim does not clear issues.route, and publishClaimant/primaryAuthorsIssueOf skip whenever a route is set, so a stale self-route sends every later person's comment to the released session and never to the next claimant or the spec's writers.

The before/after load was measured at 4c3eb5caf, before ccc0e3b5 added loadPrimaryDocumentAuthors, and the comment-replies load uses claimed issues only, so the second batch query never runs. The PR body's 'no measurable cost' does not cover the head; re-measure at the corrective head with unclaimed, unrouted issues in the load.

'A comment that mentions you arrives once, as the mention' and 'in an ask's thread too, so a mentioned session hears the comment once' are false for an ask follower: publishFollowerRoutes never reads suppressed_authors (packages/envoy/AGENTS.md says so), and validateCommentMentions allows mentions on ask replies.

'the reopen that a reply makes in the same transaction tells no session twice' contradicts publisher_comment_recipients_test.go:210-214, where the root author gets both the reopen and the reply; AGENTS.md's 'no new session twice' is accurate.

'A routed issue still reaches only its route' is false: on a routed issue a person's reply also reaches the thread's sessions and the thread document's sessions (publishAuthorRoutes ignores the route; test case 'a routed issue reaches the route's holder and the thread's sessions').

fastFollow: Deduplicate the outbox recipient routing: one resolver-computed claim-recipient list sharing publishAuthorRoutes' actor/suppression filter, one keyed-sessions loader, drop publishClaimant's unreachable actor skip and its forced-notify test cases; split report.ts by its banner sections with a first-match class chain.
